title: Loose Rein reviews.yaml
description: Which reviews this repository runs: the adversarial review before the mandate, stage by stage, the reviewer steps that read each batch of tasks, and the reviews of the whole change read before acceptance. Outside the mandate's freeze on purpose — which tool raises the quality of the work is inside what the mandate delegates, not part of what it decides — and written only by `rein reviews apply` at a terminal or by the dashboard's write session, each change recorded in the audit chain with the whole document it wrote, which is what the file on disk is checked against. The comparison acceptance rests on is not here and cannot be put here: it is what a human decides by, not a way of improving the work.

adversarial.description: Whether the fresh-context adversarial review runs before the mandate, per drafting stage. A stage set to false is named on the mandate's approval screen.

steps.description: The reviewer steps of the quality gate. Each is one reviewer launch per batch (and per join, by `stage`), reading for every review it lists. Empty: no reviewer reads the code before acceptance.

reviews.description: What this step reads for: `adversarial`, `correctness`, `simplification`, `security`, or the name of an entry under `custom`.

retries.description: How many times a task sent back with this step's `must_fix` findings is read again before it stops.

stage.description: `task` reads each batch before it merges; `integration` reads every join; `both` (the default) reads each batch, and a join whose merge had to resolve a conflict.

paths.description: Glob patterns restricting this step to tasks whose changed files match at least one. Absent: every task.

whole_change.description: Reviews of the whole change: read once every task has merged and before acceptance, because what one task leaves open and another path reaches is only in the merged tree. Their findings are repaired by the loop like any other; what reaches acceptance is only what no repair could close. `security`: whether a security reviewer reads it. Off, the review records that it took no security reading, a blocking finding an earlier reading recorded still stands until its anchored code is gone or a human disputes it, and acceptance says the reading was not taken.

custom.description: Reviews beyond the packaged four: a name, and the question the reviewer reads for. The question is held here rather than in a file of its own so that what a review asks is written by the same person, through the same path, and bound by the same record as whether it runs.

repoPath.description: A repo-relative POSIX path: no absolute form, no `..` segment, no empty segment, no backslash, no control character, no leading `-`.
